newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-Auckland have to improve to take shield.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Auckland have to improve to take shield.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 16 - A repetition of Auckland's poor performance in the 30-10 victory over Canterbury in their NPC first division rugby match on Saturday would not win them the Ranfurly Shield on October 4, NZPA reports.
Both coach Graham Henry and stand-in captain Eroni Clarke admitted after Saturday's display that Auckland had a lot of improving to do if they were to take back the shield from Waikato.
Waikato looked every bit the champions in seeing off North Harbour 17-14 in their first shield defence last Friday night.

Despite the fact they scored four quick tries in a 10-minute period just before halftime with winger Brian Lima bagging two, Auckland were simply ordinary for the rest of the match against Canterbury.
They failed to put any points on the board in the second half and seemed content to allow Canterbury to establish an edge over them.
Henry said he didn't know why his team were so flat and conceded they would have to lift their game enormously to match Waikato.
"I thought Waikato played very well on Friday night. They had the possession and every time I looked at the TV Mark Cooksley seemed to be up in the air grabbing the pill," Henry said.
"They played the game correctly against North Harbour because they threw the ball a lot in the lineouts and fed the scrums.
"It was a huge occasion and the Ranfurly Shield seems to do something for the rest of New Zealand which is great."
Henry said his team were aware they might get a chance to retrieve the Ranfurly Shield, which they lost to Taranaki last month.
"We hadn't given it a great deal of thought but it was always a possibility, and it was there at the back of the mind that it would come up again and we'd have another crack at it," he said.

Clarke, who took over the captaincy of Auckland when flanker Michael Jones left the field injured midway through the second half on Saturday, sees the shield challenge as a chance for his side to redeem themselves.
Clarke led Auckland when they lost the shield to Taranaki.
"It could be a chance to make amends, especially for a lot of the boys who are playing," he said.
"Challenging for the Ranfurly Shield lifts the guys. It would lift any challenger and it will be good to be the challenging side again so we'll see how we go.
"We have to improve a whole lot," Clarke said.
